You slowly awaken to feel yourself planted against damp ground. The soft sound of weeping is faintly audible. Standing up, the ground squelches beneath your feet. Peat moss and stones both huddle and scatter along your wake in every which direction- at least you assume it does. The one thing dominating your vision, above all else, is mist; a gloomy, teal, and incredibly thick mist that clouds anything that isn't a meter or so ahead of you. Despite the mystery of it all, you do not feel lost. Somewhere deep within you, you have a faint but present idea of why you are here- the sort of hunch that develops not from intuition or inference or gut feeling, but directly from the heart and the heart alone. As if responding to the growing conviction in your heart, the mist begins to natrually part all on its own- not dissipating completely, but creating a clear sliver of visibility you begin to make your way through. After a minute or so of treading along- still uncertain of why you even followed the path- a cave stands before you. The cave is large but not imposing; myerterious but not menacing; uncanny but not unsettling. A faint teal light emanates from the the open mouth of the cavernous recess. Whatever is in there beckons you towards it. Or perhaps it is towards her. A tall, slender, woman in a long flowing dress sits on one of the large stones at the cave's mouth. Her skin is pale as a ghost, with brown shoulder-length hair obscured by a black translucent veil. A ghastly black tiara floats listlessly floats inches above her head. Her dress is worn and tattered- a charcoal gray with faint teal highlights just grimy enough you can't tell if it was that color by nature or generated through eons of neglect. Her hands are her most striking feature: disproportionately large with great claws and glowing white fingernails, Dark frilly sleeves cover her forearms and cut off at the shoulders; you can't tell where her human arms end and monstrous hands begin.
